title: Customer-Pay Repairs Terms: Honoring the Quoted Price When the Repair Order Opens
content:
**Customer-Pay Repairs - quoted price hold.** The quoted price is honored when the repair order opens no later than the tier's quoted price hold (in days) after the estimate written date. Days are calendar days counted from the estimate written date as day zero; opening on the last day of the hold keeps the quoted price.

## Elements of the clause

- **Event the clock starts from**: the estimate written date, as recorded on the Repair Estimates & Appointments booking that the Customer-Pay Repairs repair order converts. That system record, matched by the booking being converted, is what decides the date; the date is checked before the repair order is opened.
- **Counting**: calendar days, with the estimate written date as day zero; day one is the next calendar day.
- **Comparison**: the opening date must be no later than the last day of the hold.
- **Boundary**: inclusive. Opening on the last day of the hold keeps the quoted price.
- **Length of the hold**: the tier's quoted price hold in calendar days.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Tier hold | Estimate written (day zero) | Last day of the hold | Repair order opens | Quoted price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-04-01 (day 30) | 2026-04-01 | Honored: opening on the last day keeps it |
| 30 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-04-01 (day 30) | 2026-04-02 (day 31) | Opening falls after the hold |
| 60 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-05-01 (day 60) | 2026-05-01 | Honored |
| 60 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-05-01 (day 60) | 2026-04-15 (day 44) | Honored |

## Points of judgement

- Counting runs on calendar days, so weekends and month ends count like any other day: from a 2026-03-02 written date, 30 days ends on 2026-04-01 because March has 31 days.
- The date that matters is the opening date of the Customer-Pay Repairs repair order, not the date on which the customer first asks about it.
